items.stem: EARTH SCIENCE : An earthquake emits a primary wave and a secondary wave. Near the surface of the Earth the primary wave travels at about 5 miles per second and the secondary wave at about 3 miles per second. From the time lag between the two waves arriving at a given receiving station, it is possible to estimate the distance to the quake. (The epicenter can be located by obtaining distance bearings at three or more stations.) Suppose a station measured a time difference of 16 seconds between the arrival of the two waves. (i) How long did each wave travel? (ii) How far was the earthquake from the station?
items.answer: Let p represent the time of the primary wave and s the time of the secondary wave. The time difference is 16 seconds, so s − p = 16 ...(1). Using Distance = Rate × Time, the distance for the primary wave = 5p and for the secondary wave = 3s. These distances are equal, so 5p = 3s ...(2). From (1), s = p + 16; substituting in (2): 5p = 3(p + 16) ⟹ 5p = 3p + 48 ⟹ 2p = 48 ⟹ p = 24 seconds, and s = 24 + 16 = 40 seconds. The distance travelled is 5p = 120 miles. (i) The primary wave travelled 24 seconds and the secondary wave 40 seconds. (ii) The earthquake was 120 miles from the station.
items.ocr: The printed number '123.' sits a few characters before this slice's start; the stem was recovered in full from the markdown. LaTeX arrays in the solution ('D i s t a n c e = R a t e × T i m e') rewritten to Unicode.

items.stem: Architectural Wonders : When it was first constructed in 1889, the Eiffel Tower in Paris, France, was the tallest structure in the world. In 1975, the CN Tower in Toronto, Canada, became the world's tallest structure. The CN Tower is 153 ft less than twice the height of the Eiffel Tower, and the sum of their heights is 2799 ft. (i) How tall is CN tower? (ii) How tall is Eiffel tower?
items.answer: Let the heights of the Eiffel Tower and the CN Tower be x and y respectively. The CN Tower is 153 ft less than twice the height of the Eiffel Tower, so 2x − y = 153 ...(1). The sum of their heights is 2799 ft, so x + y = 2799 ...(2). Adding (1) and (2): 3x = 2952 ⟹ x = 984. Substituting x = 984 in (2): y = 2799 − 984 = 1815. (i) The height of the CN Tower is 1815 ft. (ii) The height of the Eiffel Tower is 984 ft.

items.stem: TOWER OF PISA : To prove that objects of different weights fall at the same rate, Galileo dropped two objects with different weights from the Leaning Tower of Pisa in Italy. The objects hit the ground at the same time. An object dropped off the top of Leaning Tower of Pisa falls vertically with constant acceleration. If s is the distance of the object above the ground (in feet) t seconds after its release, then s and t are related by an equation of the form s = a + bt², where a and b are constants. Suppose the object is 180 feet above the ground 1 second after its release and 132 feet above the ground 2 seconds after its release. (i) Find the constants a and b. (ii) How high is the Leaning Tower of Pisa? (iii) How long does the object fall?
items.answer: We have s = a + bt². (i) When t = 1, s = 180, so 180 = a + b(1)² ⟹ 180 = a + b ...(1). When t = 2, s = 132, so 132 = a + b(2)² ⟹ 132 = a + 4b ...(2). Subtracting (1) from (2): −48 = 3b ⟹ b = −16. Substituting in (1): 180 = a − 16 ⟹ a = 196. Thus a = 196 and b = −16. (ii) The height of the building is s when t = 0. Since s = 196 − 16t², at t = 0 we get s = 196 feet. (iii) The object falls until s = 0: 0 = 196 − 16t² ⟹ 16t² = 196 ⟹ t² = 196/16 ⟹ t = 14/4 = 3.5 seconds.
items.ocr: The final printed line is truncated to 't = 14/4 = 3.5 se'; completed to 3.5 seconds.

items.stem: Jyoti Kumari is an Indian student from Sirhulli in the rural Darbhanga district of Bihar. She came to notice after she bicycled some 1,200 km with her injured father to reach their home village during COVID-19 lockdowns in India. This act of bravery was praised by the Senior Advisor to the President of the United States, Ivanka Trump, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. She was given a national award, and a Bollywood film was proposed to record her story. Jyoti travelled 90 km every day to reach her home town in Harbin. One day, when she started, after riding a certain distance, she stopped for some time to repair her bicycle. After which she completes the whole journey of 90 km at half speed in 12 hours. If the breakdown had occurred 10 km farther off, she would have done the whole journey in 11 hours. (i) Find where the breakdown occurred. (ii) Find her original speed.
items.answer: Let x be the distance of the place where the breakdown occurred and y her original speed. She rides x km at speed y and the remaining (90 − x) km at half speed y/2, taking 12 hours: x/y + (90 − x)/(y/2) = 12 ⟹ x + 180 − 2x = 12y ⟹ x + 12y = 180 ...(1). If the breakdown had occurred 10 km farther off: (x + 10)/y + (90 − (x + 10))/(y/2) = 11 ⟹ x + 10 + 180 − 2(x + 10) = 11y ⟹ −x + 170 = 11y ⟹ x + 11y = 170 ...(2). Subtracting (2) from (1): y = 10 km/hr. From (2): x + 11 × 10 = 170 ⟹ x = 60 km. (i) The breakdown occurred at 60 km. (ii) Her original speed was 10 km/hr.
items.ocr: MinerU wrecked the worked solution ('x + 1^100 − 2x = 12', 'x + 11 + 180 − 2x − 21 = 11y', '(x + 101)/y'); every equation was recovered from the PDF text layer (scripts.textlayer --chapter 3 --question 126). The stem's 'repair his bicycle' read as 'her bicycle'.

items.stem: At some point, it's time to kick, or gently ease, kids off the parental gravy train. The circle graph shows the percentage of parents who think significant financial support should end at various milestones. The difference in the percentage who would end this support after completing college and after completing high school is 6%. (i) Find the percentage of parents who would end financial support after a child completes college. (ii) Find the percentage of parents who would end financial support after a child completes high school.
items.answer: Let x% of parents end support after college and y% after high school. The remaining slices of the circle graph account for 30%, 6% and 14%, so x + y + 30 + 6 + 14 = 100 ⟹ x + y + 50 = 100 ⟹ x + y = 50 ...(1). The difference between the two percentages is 6%, so x − y = 6 ...(2). Adding (1) and (2): 2x = 56 ⟹ x = 28. Substituting x = 28 in (1): y = 50 − 28 = 22. (i) 28% of parents would end financial support after a child completes college. (ii) 22% of parents would end financial support after a child completes high school.
items.ocr: The values 30, 6 and 14 used in the first equation are read off the printed circle graph; the running text never repeats them, so the figure is required.

items.stem: Cash Register Malfunction : You are the manager of a shoe store. On Sunday morning you are going over the receipts for the previous week's sales. A total of 320 pairs of cross-training shoes were sold. One style sold for Rs 1135 and the other sold for Rs 1495. The total receipts were Rs 420,480. The cash register that was supposed to keep track of the number of each type of shoe sold malfunctioned. Can you recover the information? If so, how many of each type were sold?
items.answer: Let x and y be the numbers of pairs of the two styles sold. Since a total of 320 pairs were sold, x + y = 320 ...(1). Taking the prices used in the worked solution, Rs 1139 and Rs 1459, the receipts give 1139x + 1459y = 420480 ...(2). Substituting y = 320 − x from (1) in (2): 1139x + 1459(320 − x) = 420480 ⟹ 1139x + 466880 − 1459x = 420480 ⟹ −320x = −46400 ⟹ x = 145. Substituting x = 145 in (1): y = 320 − 145 = 175. So 145 and 175 pairs of shoes of style one and style two were sold.
items.ocr: The stem prints the prices as Rs 1135 and Rs 1495 but the worked solution uses Rs 1139 and Rs 1459. Only the solution's figures reproduce the printed total (1139 × 145 + 1459 × 175 = 420480), so the solution wins; the stem is left exactly as printed. The PDF text layer shows the same mismatch, so it is the book's own error rather than OCR damage.

items.stem: Hostel Life : Banasthali Vidyapith is a fully residential women's university offering courses from primary to Ph.D. level. It offers a number of UG, PG, and Doctoral level Programs under various Departments. Admission to the same is done on the basis of merit scored in qualifying examination, however, for some courses, an aptitude test is also conducted at the university level. Swati is doing M.Sc. in biotechnology from Banasthali Vidyapith and lives in the university hostel. A part of monthly hostel charge is fixed and the remaining depends on the number of days one has taken food in the mess. When Swati takes food for 18 days, she has to pay Rs. 5160 as hostel charges whereas Taniya who takes food for 23 days pays Rs. 5760 as hostel charges. (i) Find the fixed charges of hostel. (ii) Find the cost of food per day.
items.answer: Let the fixed charge be x and the cost of food per day be y. Then x + 18y = 5160 ...(1) and x + 23y = 5760 ...(2). Subtracting (1) from (2): 5y = 600 ⟹ y = 120. Substituting y = 120 in (1): x + 18 × 120 = 5160 ⟹ x = 5160 − 2160 = 3000. (i) The fixed charge of the hostel is Rs 3000. (ii) The cost of food per day is Rs 120.
items.ocr: OCR drop-outs in the stem repaired: 'Swati s doing MSc. in biotechnology from Banastli Vidyapith' → 'Swati is doing M.Sc. in biotechnology from Banasthali Vidyapith'; 'Taniya who takes food for 23 days Rs. 5760' given its missing verb 'pays'.

items.stem: Uniform motion with current : (R + C)t = d (With the current); (R − C)t = d (Against the current). The formula shown can be used to solve uniform motion problems involving a current, where d represents distance travelled, R is the rate of the object with no current, C is the speed of the current, and t is the time. Vibhur rows 9 km up river (against the current) in 3 hr. It only took him 1 hr to row 5 km downstream (with the current). (i) How fast was the current? (ii) How fast can he row in still water?
items.answer: Vibhur rows 9 km up river (against the current) in 3 hr, so (R − C)3 = 9 ⟹ R − C = 3 ...(1). It took him 1 hr to row 5 km downstream (with the current), so (R + C)1 = 5 ⟹ R + C = 5 ...(2). Adding (1) and (2): 2R = 8 ⟹ R = 4. Substituting R = 4 in (2): C = 1. (i) The current was 1 km/h. (ii) He can row 4 km/h in still water.
items.ocr: The two formulas were printed as a LaTeX array and rewritten to Unicode. This question carries no figure of its own.

items.stem: Canoeing on a stream : On a recent camping trip, it took Mohinder and Aslam 2 hr to row 4 mi upstream from the drop in point to the camp site. After a leisurely weekend of camping, fishing, and relaxation, they rowed back downstream to the drop in point in just 30 min. Use this information to find (i) Find the speed of the current. (ii) Find the speed Mohinder and Aslam would be rowing in still water.
items.answer: Let c represent the speed of the current and s the speed of the boat in still water. Going upstream to the camp site: (s − c)2 = 4 ⟹ s − c = 2 ...(1). Returning downstream in 30 min = 1/2 hr: (s + c)(1/2) = 4 ⟹ s + c = 8 ...(2). Adding (1) and (2): 2s = 10 ⟹ s = 5. Substituting s = 5 in (2): c = 3. (i) The speed of the current is 3 mph. (ii) They would row at 5 mph in still water.
items.ocr: The last printed line reads '5 mpl'; read as 5 mph.

items.stem: Luxury Cruise : As India's first domestic cruise liner, Angriya has made many voyages on the Mumbai-Goa sea route, along the pristine Konkan Coast. It has given India and Indians a sense of pride and happiness, while introducing the travelers to coral diversity and royal sea forts along the way. Last year we enjoyed our summer vacation at Angriya cruise. From Mumbai to the Goa, with the current the trip took 70 hr. After a few days of fun in the sun, the ship leaves for Mumbai, against the current with the return trip taking 82 hr. (i) Find the speed of the current. (ii) Find the cruising speed of the ship.
items.answer: Let c represent the speed of the current and s the cruising speed of the ship; the Mumbai–Goa distance used in the printed solution is 1435 km. Trip to Goa: (s + c)70 = 1435 ⟹ 2s + 2c = 41 ...(1). Return to Mumbai: (s − c)82 = 1435 ⟹ 2s − 2c = 35 ...(2). Adding (1) and (2): 4s = 76 ⟹ s = 19 kmph. Subtracting (2) from (1): 4c = 6 ⟹ c = 1.5 kmph. (i) The speed of the current is 1.5 kmph. (ii) The cruising speed of the ship is 19 kmph.
items.ocr: The stem never states the Mumbai–Goa distance; the 1435 km used in the working is taken from the printed solution. The book's last line prints 's = 1.5 kmph' where it must read c = 1.5 kmph (the PDF text layer prints the same slip); corrected here.

items.stem: Point of No Return : The point during a flight at which an aircraft is no longer capable of returning to the airfield from which it took off due to fuel considerations. Beyond this point the aircraft must proceed to some other destination. A plane carries enough fuel for 20 hours of flight at an airspeed of 150 miles per hour. How far can it fly into a 30 mph headwind and still have enough fuel to return to its starting point?
items.answer: Let t₁ represent the time taken flying out; the distance travelled out is (150 − 30)t₁. Let t₂ represent the time taken to return; the distance travelled back is (150 + 30)t₂. These two distances are equal, so (150 − 30)t₁ = (150 + 30)t₂ ⟹ 120t₁ = 180t₂ ⟹ 2t₁ = 3t₂ ⟹ t₁ = 1.5t₂. Since there is fuel for a total flight of 20 hours, t₁ + t₂ = 20 ⟹ 1.5t₂ + t₂ = 20 ⟹ 2.5t₂ = 20 ⟹ t₂ = 20/2.5 = 8 hours. Distance travelled in the 8-hour return flight = (150 + 30) × 8 = 1,440 miles. So the plane can fly 1,440 miles into the headwind.

items.stem: Computing a Refund : The grocery store we use does not mark prices on its goods. My wife went to this store, purchased three 1-kg packages of almond and two 500-gram packages cashew, and paid a total of Rs 1345. Not knowing that she went to the store, I also went to the same store, purchased two 1-kg packages of almond and three 500-gram packages cashew, and paid a total of Rs 1145. Now we want to return two 1-kg packages of almond and two 500-gram packages cashew. How much will be refunded?
items.answer: Let x and y be the price of a 1-kg package of almond and a 500-gram package of cashew. My wife's purchase gives 3x + 2y = 1345 ...(1) and mine gives 2x + 3y = 1145 ...(2). Multiplying (1) by 3 and (2) by 2: 9x + 6y = 4035 ...(3) and 4x + 6y = 2290 ...(4). Subtracting (4) from (3): 5x = 1745 ⟹ x = 349. Substituting x = 349 in (1): 3 × 349 + 2y = 1345 ⟹ 2y = 298 ⟹ y = 149. So one 1-kg package of almond costs Rs 349 and one 500-gram package of cashew costs Rs 149. Returning two almond and two cashew packages refunds 2x + 2y = 2 × 349 + 2 × 149 = Rs 996.
items.ocr: The printed solution writes 'Substituting x = 34.9' and says it substitutes into eq (2) while it actually substitutes into eq (1); read as x = 349 into eq (1), which the very next printed line, 3 × 349 + 2y = 1345, confirms.

items.stem: Financial Planning : Planning for retirement starts with thinking about your retirement goals and how long you have to meet them. Then you need to look at the types of retirement accounts that can help you raise the money to fund your future. As you save that money, you have to invest it to enable it to grow. A recently retired couple needs Rs 120,000 per year to supplement their Social Security. They have Rs 1,500,000 to invest to obtain this income. They have decided on two investment options: AA bonds yielding 10% per annum and a fixed deposit yielding 5%. (i) How much should be invested in each to realize exactly Rs 120,000? (ii) If, after 2 years, the couple requires Rs 140,000 per year in income, how should they reallocate their investment to achieve the new amount?
items.answer: Let x and y be the amounts, in thousands of rupees, invested in AA bonds and the fixed deposit. Since Rs 1,500,000 = 1500 thousand is available, x + y = 1500 ...(1). (i) For an income of Rs 120,000 = 120 thousand: (10/100)x + (5/100)y = 120 ⟹ 2x + y = 2400 ...(2). Subtracting (1) from (2): x = 900, so y = 1500 − 900 = 600. Rs 900 thousand should be invested in AA bonds and Rs 600 thousand in the fixed deposit. (ii) For an income of Rs 140,000 = 140 thousand: (10/100)x + (5/100)y = 140 ⟹ 2x + y = 2800 ...(4), together with x + y = 1500 ...(3). Subtracting (3) from (4): x = 1300, so y = 1500 − 1300 = 200. They should reallocate to Rs 1300 thousand in AA bonds and Rs 200 thousand in the fixed deposit.
items.ocr: In part (i) the printed working jumps from (10/100)x + (5/100)y = 120 straight to 'Subtracting eq (1) from (2)'; the intermediate line 2x + y = 2400 is restored (part (ii) prints its matching 2x + y = 2800).

items.stem: Actual Number of Calories : University of Arkansas researchers discovered that we underestimate the number of calories in restaurant meals. The next time you eat out, take the number of calories you think you ate and double it. The researchers concluded that this number should be a more accurate estimate. The actual number of calories in one portion of hamburger and fries and two portions of pizza is 4240. The actual number of calories in two portions of hamburger and fries and one portion of pizza is 3980. (i) Find the actual number of calories in one portion of hamburger and fries. (ii) Find the actual number of calories in one portion of pizza.
items.answer: Let the number of calories in one portion of hamburger and fries be x and in one portion of pizza be y. Then x + 2y = 4240 ...(1) and 2x + y = 3980 ...(2). Multiplying (1) by 2 and subtracting (2) from it: 4y − y = 2 × 4240 − 3980 ⟹ 3y = 4500 ⟹ y = 1500. Substituting y = 1500 in (2): 2x = 3980 − 1500 = 2480 ⟹ x = 1240. (i) One portion of hamburger and fries has 1240 calories. (ii) One portion of pizza has 1500 calories.
items.ocr: A stray '∴' printed after the title was dropped. The substitution step arrived as a broken array (', 0 0 / 2x / 2x = 3980 − 1500 = 2480'); restored to 2x = 2480 ⟹ x = 1240, which matches the printed answer.

items.stem: Presale Order : A wireless store owner takes presale orders for a new smartphone and tablet. He gets 340 preorders for the smartphone and 250 preorders for the tablet. The combined value of the preorders is Rs 27,050,000. The price of a smartphone and tablet together is Rs 96500. (i) How much does smartphone cost? (ii) How much does tablet cost?
items.answer: Let x and y be the prices of a smartphone and a tablet. The combined value of 340 smartphones and 250 tablets is Rs 27,050,000, so 340x + 250y = 27050000 ...(1). The price of a smartphone and a tablet together is Rs 96500, so x + y = 96500 ...(2). Substituting y = 96500 − x from (2) in (1): 340x + 250(96500 − x) = 27050000 ⟹ 340x + 24125000 − 250x = 27050000 ⟹ 90x = 2925000 ⟹ x = 32500. Substituting x = 32500 in (2): y = 96500 − 32500 = 64000. (i) A smartphone costs Rs 32500. (ii) A tablet costs Rs 64000.
items.ocr: MinerU dropped the line '90x = 2925000 ⟹ x = 32500' between the expansion and the back substitution; restored from the PDF text layer.

items.stem: MASK : Masks are an additional step to help prevent people from getting and spreading COVID-19. They provide a barrier that keeps respiratory droplets from spreading. Wear a mask and take every day preventive actions in public settings. Due to ongoing Corona virus outbreak, Wellness Medical store has started selling masks of decent quality. The store is selling two types of masks currently type A and type B. The cost of type A mask is Rs. 15 and of type B mask is Rs. 20. In the month of April, 2020, the store sold 100 masks for total sales of Rs. 1650. (i) How many masks of each type were sold in the month of April? (ii) If the store had sold 50 masks of each type, what would be its sales in the month of April? (iii) Due to great demand and short supply, the store has increased the price of each type by Rs. 5 from May 1, 2020. In the month of May, 2020, the store sold 310 masks for total sales of Rs. 6875. How many masks of each type were sold in the month of May? (iv) What percent of masks of each type sale was increased in the month of May, compared with the sale of month April? (v) What extra profit did store earn by increasing price in May month?
items.answer: (i) Let x be the number of type A masks and y the number of type B masks sold in April. Then x + y = 100 ...(1) and 15x + 20y = 1650 ...(2). Multiplying (1) by 15 and subtracting from (2): 5y = 150 ⟹ y = 30, so x = 70. Hence 70 masks of type A and 30 masks of type B were sold. (ii) Total sales = 50 × 15 + 50 × 20 = Rs 1750. (iii) In May the prices become Rs 20 and Rs 25. With x + y = 310 and 20x + 25y = 6875, multiplying the first by 20 and subtracting it from the second: 5y = 675 ⟹ y = 135 and x = 310 − 135 = 175. So 175 type A and 135 type B masks were sold. (iv) Increase in type A = (175 − 70)/70 × 100 = 150%; increase in type B = (135 − 30)/30 × 100 = 350%. (v) Total sale value in May at the old prices = 175 × 15 + 135 × 20 = 5325 and at the new prices = 6875, so extra profit = 6875 − 5325 = Rs 1550. Alternatively the extra profit is Rs 5 per mask on 310 masks = 310 × 5 = Rs 1550.
items.ocr: Part (i)'s elimination arrived as a broken array ('5y / x = 150 ⟹ y = 30'); read as 5y = 150. The '(ii)' label is missing before 'Total Sales'. Part (iv) prints the type B increase as (105 − 30)/30 × 100, but 135 type B masks were sold in May and the printed result 350% follows from (135 − 30)/30, so 135 is used. Part (iii) of the printed solution repeats the word 'April' where it means May.

items.stem: Wilt Chamberlain : Wilton Norman "Wilt" Chamberlain was an American basketball player, and played in the NBA during the 1960s. At 7 feet 1 inch, he was the tallest and heaviest player in the league for most of his career, and he was one of the most famous people in the game for many years. He is the first and only basketball player to score 100 points in an NBA game. In the 1961–1962 NBA basketball season, Wilt Chamberlain of the Philadelphia Warriors made 30 baskets. Some of the baskets were free throws (worth 1 point each) and some were field goals (worth 2 points each). The number of field goals was 10 more than the number of free throws. (i) How many field goals did he make? (ii) How many free throws did he make? (iii) What was the total number of points scored? (iv) If Wilt Chamberlain played 5 games during this season, what was the average number of points per game? (v) If Wilt Chamberlain played 10 games during this season, what was the average number of points per game?
items.answer: (i) Let x be the number of free throws and y the number of field goals. Then x + y = 30 and y = x + 10. Solving these, x = 10 and y = 20, so he made 20 field goals. (ii) He made 10 free throws. (iii) Points scored = 10 × 1 + 2 × 20 = 50. (iv) Over 5 games the average = 50/5 = 10 points per game. (v) Over 10 games the average = 50/10 = 5 points per game.
items.ocr: The two averages arrived as collapsed fractions ('(iv)Average point 50 = 10 50' and '(v) Average point = 5 10'); read from the PDF text layer as 50/5 = 10 and 50/10 = 5.

items.stem: Architect : An architect is a skilled professional who plans and designs buildings and generally plays a key role in their construction. Architects are highly trained in the art and science of building design. Since they bear responsibility for the safety of their buildings' occupants, architects must be professionally licensed. Varsha is a licensed architect and designs very innovative houses. She has made a house layout for her client which is given below. In the layout, the design and measurements have been made such that area of two bedrooms and kitchen together is 95 sq. m. (i) Which pair of linear equations does describe this situation? (ii) What is the length of the outer boundary of the layout? (iii) What is the area of bedroom 1? (iv) What is the area of living room in the layout? (v) What is the cost of laying tiles in Kitchen at the rate of Rs. 50 per sq. m?
items.answer: (i) Area of the two bedrooms = 5x + 5x = 10x m² and area of the kitchen = 5y m². Since together they are 95 sq. m, 10x + 5y = 95 ⟹ 2x + y = 19. Also from the figure, x + 2 + y = 15 ⟹ x + y = 13. (ii) Length of the outer boundary = 2(5 + 2 + 5 + 15) = 54 m. (iii) Solving 2x + y = 19 and x + y = 13 gives x = 6 m and y = 7 m, so the area of bedroom 1 = 5 × 6 = 30 sq. m (the kitchen is 5 × 7 = 35 sq. m). (iv) Area of the living room = (15 × 7) − 30 = 105 − 30 = 75 m². (v) Area of the kitchen = 7 × 5 = 35 sq. m, so the cost of laying tiles = 50 × 35 = Rs 1750.
items.ocr: The dimensions 5 m, 2 m and 15 m used throughout the solution appear only in the printed house-layout figure, so the figure is required. Stem grammar left as printed apart from 'design very innovative house' → 'designs very innovative houses' and 'measurements has been made' → 'measurements have been made'.

items.stem: Mr. RK Agrawal is owner of a famous amusement park in Delhi. The ticket charge for the park is Rs 150 for children and Rs 400 for adult. Generally he does not go to park and it is managed by team of staff. One day Mr Agrawal decided to random check the park and went there. When he checked the cash counter, he found that 480 tickets were sold and Rs 134500 was collected. (i) Let the number of children visited be x and the number of adults visited be y. Which of the following is the correct system of equations that model the problem? (ii) How many children visited the park? (iii) How many adults visited the park? (iv) How much amount collected if 300 children and 350 adults visited the park? (v) One day total visited children and adults together is 750 and the total amount collected is Rs 212500. What are the number of children and adults visited the park?
items.answer: (i) Since 480 people visited, x + y = 480. Since Rs 134500 was collected, 150x + 400y = 134500 ⟹ 3x + 8y = 2690. (ii) Solving x + y = 480 and 3x + 8y = 2690 gives x = 230 and y = 250, so the number of children who attended is 230. (iii) The number of adults who visited the park is 250. (iv) Amount = 150 × 300 + 400 × 350 = Rs 185000. (v) Solving x + y = 750 and 150x + 400y = 212500 ⟹ 3x + 8y = 4250 gives x = 350 and y = 400, i.e. 350 children and 400 adults visited the park.

items.stem: Dipesh bought 3 notebooks and 2 pens for Rs. 80. His friend Ramesh said that price of each notebook could be Rs. 25. Then three notebooks would cost Rs. 75, the two pens would cost Rs. 5 and each pen could be for Rs. 2.50. Another friend Amar felt that Rs. 2.50 for one pen was too little. It should be at least Rs. 16. Then the price of each notebook would also be Rs. 16. Aditya also bought the same types of notebooks and pens as Dipesh. He paid Rs. 110 for 4 notebooks and 3 pens. (i) Whether the estimation of Ramesh and Amar is applicable for Aditya? (ii) Let the cost of one notebook be x and that of pen be y. Which of the following set describe the given problem? (iii) What is the exact cost of the notebook? (iv) What is the exact cost of the pen? (v) What is the total cost if they purchase the same type of 15 notebooks and 12 pens?
items.answer: (i) Consider Ramesh's prices. If one notebook is Rs. 25 and one pen is Rs. 2.50, the cost of 4 notebooks is 4 × 25 = Rs 100 and the cost of 3 pens is 3 × 2.50 = Rs 7.50, so Aditya should have paid 100 + 7.50 = Rs 107.50. He paid Rs 110, so Ramesh's estimation is wrong. Now consider Amar's prices, Rs. 16 each. The cost of 4 notebooks is 4 × 16 = Rs 64 and the cost of 3 pens is 3 × 16 = Rs 48, so Aditya should have paid 64 + 48 = Rs 112, which is more than he actually paid. Therefore Amar's estimation is also wrong. (ii) 3x + 2y = 80 and 4x + 3y = 110. (iii) Solving 3x + 2y = 80 and 4x + 3y = 110 gives x = 20 and y = 10, so one notebook costs Rs 20. (iv) One pen costs Rs 10. (v) Total cost = 15 × 20 + 12 × 10 = Rs 420.
items.ocr: The book prints '3 × 16 = 64' for the cost of three pens and then adds '64 + 48 = 112'; 48 is the correct value and the 64 is the book's own slip (the PDF text layer prints the same). Corrected in the answer.

items.stem:
Jodhpur is the second-largest city in the Indian state of Rajasthan and officially the second metropolitan city of the state. Jodhpur was historically the capital of the Kingdom of Marwar, which is now part of Rajasthan. Jodhpur is a popular tourist destination, featuring many palaces, forts, and temples, set in the stark landscape of the Thar Desert. It is popularly known as the "Blue City" among people of Rajasthan and all over India. The old city circles the Mehrangarh Fort and is bounded by a wall with several gates. The city has expanded greatly outside the wall, though, over the past several decades. Jodhpur is also known for the rare breed of horses known as Marwari or Malani, which are only found here. Last year we visited Jodhpur in a group of 25 friends. When we went Mehrangarh fort we found following fare for ride :
RideNormal Hours FarePeak Hours Fare
HorseRs 503 Times
ElephantRs 1002 Times
Some people choose to ride on horse and rest choose to ride on elephant. (i) First day we rode in normal hours and we paid Rs 1950 for ride. Let x be the number of horses hired and y be the number elephants hired. Which of the following is the correct system of equation that model the problem? (ii) How many horses were hired? (iii) How many elephant were hired? (iv) Next day we rode in peak hours, then how much total fare was paid by our group? (v) What was the increase in total fare because of peak hours ride?
items.answer: (i) Let x be the number of horses hired and y the number of elephants hired. Then x + y = 25 and 50x + 100y = 1950 ⟹ x + 2y = 39. (ii) Solving x + y = 25 and x + 2y = 39 gives x = 11 and y = 14, so the number of horses hired is 11. (iii) The number of elephants hired is 14. (iv) In peak hours the horse fare is 3 times and the elephant fare 2 times the normal fare, so the horse riding fare = 3 × 50 × 11 = Rs 1650 and the elephant riding fare = 2 × 100 × 14 = Rs 2800, giving a total fare = 1650 + 2800 = Rs 4450. (v) Total fare in normal hours = Rs 1950 and in peak hours = Rs 4450, so the extra fare = 4450 − 1950 = Rs 2500.
